newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares fall at noon ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares fall at noon ahead of holiday.

text.p: Shenzhen's foreign currency B share market fell slightly at midday on Thursday, with a wait-and-see mood prevailing ahead of the long holiday, brokers said.
The B share index lost 0.45 points or 0.31 percent to 144.08 on thin turnover of HK$20 million.
The domestic A share index slipped 3.54 points or 0.76 percent to 459.67 on turnover of 4.7 billion yuan as newcomers diverted some speculative funds out of existing shares, brokers said.
"B share investors were seen to be reluctant to buy right before the long holiday," an analyst with a major Chinese brokerage said.
The Shenzhen Stock Exchange has announced it will close on June 30 and July 1 to mark the Hong Kong handover and trading will resume on Wednesday July 2.
Rumours that Beijing was planning to introduce new measures to further counter stock speculation in July also hurt sentiment, brokers said.
They said they expected cautious sentiment to extend into this afternoon and Friday.
Automobile parts maker Wuxi Weifu was the worst B share performer, declining HK$0.40 or 8.00 percent to HK$4.60.
Seven companies listed a combined 340 million A shares in Shenzhen on Thursday, a daily record for south China bourse, brokers said.
They all posted strong debuts, which attracted many investors, they said.
New listings are not calculated into the stock indices on their first day of trading.
Petrochemical concern Yueyang Xingchang was the weakest A share performer, sliding 3.48 yuan or 9.9 percent to 31.37 yuan.

Huludao Zinc Industry Co Ltd, the world's biggest zinc smelter, listed 90 million A shares in Shenzhen today and closed the morning session at 12.29 yuan against an issue price of 7.42 yuan. Volume reached 40 million shares, making it the most actively traded counter. (c) Reuters Limited 1997
